# Computational Evidence — Character table size of `Sₙ`

Claim under test:
`Fintype.card (ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))) = Fintype.card (Nat.Partition n)`,
i.e. the character table of the symmetric group `Sₙ` is a square matrix of side `p(n)`.

## Small-case calculations

Both sides were evaluated in Lean (`#eval`) for small `n`:

| n | `card (ConjClasses (Perm (Fin n)))` | `card (Nat.Partition n) = p(n)` |
|---|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 3 | 3 |
| 4 | 5 | 5 |
| 5 | 7 | 7 |

The two columns agree on every tested value. The cases `n = 3, 4, 5` are additionally
discharged as machine-checked `example`s in `SymmetricGroupCharacterTable.lean` via the proved
theorem `card_conjClasses_perm_fin` combined with `native_decide`.

## OEIS

The common sequence `1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15, 22, ...` is the partition numbers,
**OEIS A000041**.

## Counterexample hunt

The claim is universal over `n`. No counterexample is possible: the proved theorem
`card_conjClasses_eq_card_partition` establishes equality for every finite type `α`
(with `card α` in place of `n`), and `card_conjClasses_perm_fin` specialises it to `Sₙ`.
The injectivity half is Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.partition_eq_of_isConj`; the surjectivity half
(every partition is realised as a cycle type) is proved here in `exists_perm_cycleType`.

## Notes

The key structural fact is that conjugacy in `Sₙ` is detected exactly by cycle type, and
cycle types of permutations of an `n`-element set are in bijection with partitions of `n`.
The nontrivial direction is *realisability*: building, for an arbitrary partition, a
permutation with that exact cycle type, done by placing disjoint cycles on fresh fixed points.

Completed the research brief by formalizing, in `Algebra/PartitionConjugacyBijection.lean`, an explicit bijection between the partitions of `n` and the conjugacy classes of the symmetric group `Sₙ = Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`.

What was built (namespace `PartitionConjugacy`):

1. **Construction** (`partitionToPerm : n.Partition → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`): From a partition `p`, the permutation is built so that its disjoint cycles have lengths equal to the parts of `p` that are `≥ 2`, while parts equal to `1` become fixed points. This is obtained constructively from `Equiv.Perm.exists_with_cycleType_iff` via the helper `exists_perm_cycleType` (which shows the multiset of parts `≥ 2`, `bigParts p`, is realizable as a cycle type because its sum is `≤ n` and all entries are `≥ 2`). The realizing permutation's cycle type is recorded in `partitionToPerm_cycleType`.

2. **Well-definedness** (`partitionToPerm_partition_parts` and `permToNatPartition_partitionToPerm`): The partition of the constructed permutation (cycle lengths together with one `1` per fixed point) is exactly `p`. The core combinatorial step is `bigParts_add_replicate`: a partition equals its parts `≥ 2` plus the right number of `1`s.

3. **Constructive surjectivity** (`isConj_partitionToPerm`): For any `σ`, the permutation built from `σ`'s own partition is conjugate to `σ` (proved via equality of cycle types).

4. **The bijection** (`partitionEquivConjClasses (n) : n.Partition ≃ ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))`): forward map sends `p` to the conjugacy class of `partitionToPerm p`; inverse sends a class to the partition of any representative, well-defined using `Equiv.Perm.partition_eq_of_isConj`. # Future Directions — Character Tables of `Sₙ`

This cycle established the "column count" of the character table of the symmetric group:
the table is square of side `p(n)`, via a from-scratch proof that every partition of `n`
is realised as the cycle type of some permutation
(`Catalog/Algebra/SymmetricGroupCharacterTable.lean`,
theorem `card_conjClasses_eq_card_partition` / `card_conjClasses_perm_fin`).

Below are testable conjectures for follow-up cycles. Each is stated so that it can be turned
directly into a Lean `theorem ... := by sorry` skeleton.

## C1. Conjugacy-class size formula (Cauchy / centralizer order)
For `σ : Perm (Fin n)` with cycle type given by a partition having `m_i` parts equal to `i`,
the centralizer has order `∏_i i^{m_i} · m_i!`, and the conjugacy class of `σ` has size
`n! / ∏_i i^{m_i} · m_i!`. Testable form: the sum over conjugacy classes of these class
sizes equals `n!` (a refinement of the class equation / Burnside that re-derives `card Sₙ`).

## C2. Number of even-permutation classes splitting in `Aₙ`
A conjugacy class of `Sₙ` lying in `Aₙ` splits into two `Aₙ`-classes iff its cycle type
consists of distinct odd parts. Conjecture (testable per `n`):
`card (ConjClasses (alternatingGroup (Fin n)))`
`= card {p : Nat.Partition n // p even} + card {p : Nat.Partition n // distinct odd parts}`.

## C3. Counting permutations by number of cycles (Stirling numbers)
The number of `σ : Perm (Fin n)` with exactly `k` cycles (counting fixed points) equals the
unsigned Stirling number of the first kind `c(n,k)`. Testable form:
`∑_k c(n,k) · x^k = x (x+1) ⋯ (x+n-1)` (rising factorial), and
`∑_k c(n,k) = n!`. This connects the cycle-type stratification to a clean generating identity.

## C4. Self-conjugate partitions and the sign / number of odd-order classes
The number of self-conjugate partitions of `n` equals the number of partitions of `n` into
distinct odd parts. Bridge conjecture: this count also equals the number of conjugacy classes
of `Sₙ` on which a specified class function (e.g. a chosen real irreducible character) takes a
prescribed value — a concrete handle on symmetry of the character table.

## C5. Column sums of the character table
For any finite group, the sum of the entries in a fixed column of the character table
(indexed by `g`) equals the number of square roots of `g`, i.e. `#{x : x^2 = g}`.
Specialised to `Sₙ`: `∑_χ χ(σ) = #{τ : Perm (Fin n) | τ^2 = σ}`, and summing over all `σ`
gives `∑_χ ∑_σ χ(σ)` linked to the total number of involutions-plus-identity solutions.
Testable per `n` by `decide`/`native_decide` for small `n` before attempting the general proof.
